record.original_question: Classify the configurations of d^2 points in P^3, for d ≥ 3, such that for every general linear projection from a point x ∈ P^3, the projected configuration of d^2 points in P^2 is the complete intersection of two degree-d plane curves.

evidence.quote: Problem 15 (Francesco Polizzi, [32]) Classify the configurations of d2 points in P3, d  3, such that for every general linear projection from a point x ∈ P3, the resulting configuration of d2 points in P2 is the complete intersection of two curves of degree d.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 3$ be an integer. A finite set $Z \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ (over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero) is called $(d,d)$-geproci if for a general point $x \in \mathbb{P}^3$ the image of $Z$ under linear projection $\pi_x : \mathbb{P}^3 \dashrightarrow \mathbb{P}^2$ from $x$ is the complete intersection of two plane curves of degree $d$. A trivial example is given by an $(d,d)$-grid: a set of $d^2$ points obtained as the pairwise intersections of two families of $d$ pairwise skew lines (a "ruling-like" configuration) such that every line of one family meets every line of the other.

Classify all configurations $Z \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ of $|Z| = d^2$ points such that for every general linear projection from a point $x \in \mathbb{P}^3$, the resulting configuration of $d^2$ points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ is the complete intersection of two plane curves of degree $d$. Equivalently, describe all $(d,d)$-geproci sets of $d^2$ points in $\mathbb{P}^3$ for $d \geq 3$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is the well-known geproci classification problem. The case $d=3$ is solved: any non-degenerate set of 9 points with the property is a $(3,3)$-grid. For general $d$, classification remains open; new non-grid examples (e.g. from the $D_4$, $F_4$, and $H_4$ root systems, and a 120-point configuration) have been discovered, and partial classification results exist (e.g., under assumptions of being supported on skew lines with transversals). Active research as of 2023–2025 continues to investigate the full classification.

status_evidence.title: Geproci sets: a new perspective in algebraic geometry
status_evidence.snippet: For nine points, a non-degenerate set has a general projection that is the complete intersection of two cubics if and only if the points form a (3,3)-grid. Sets of 24 points arising from F4 also have this property.
status_evidence.claim: The d=3 case is fully solved; non-grid examples are known in higher cases.

status_evidence.title: Sets of points which project to complete intersections
status_evidence.snippet: Study of non-degenerate sets in P^3 whose general projection is a complete intersection in P^2.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on the geproci classification problem.

status_evidence.title: Geproci sets on skew lines in P^3 with two transversals
status_evidence.snippet: Classifies [m,n]-geproci sets consisting of points on skew lines with two common transversals.
status_evidence.claim: Partial classifications obtained under combinatorial hypotheses.
